test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 08 Jul, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: As of March 2020, which of the following solar power plants is the biggest plant in the world, with total installed capacity of 2,245 MW?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhadla solar park**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhadla solar park** is the biggest solar power plant in the world as of March 2020, with a total installed capacity of 2,245 MW.
 
• Located in **Rajasthan, India**, the park spreads across more than 14,000 acres in the Jodhpur district.
 
• The park has been developed in multiple phases by various developers, making it a significant contributor to India's renewable energy capacity.
 
• It plays a crucial role in India's efforts to increase the share of renewable energy in its total energy mix.
 
• The project has helped in reducing the carbon footprint and promoting sustainable development in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India has set an ambitious target to achieve **175 GW** of renewable energy capacity by 2022, out of which **100 GW** is expected to come from solar power.
 
• The **National Solar Mission**, launched in 2010, is a major initiative of the Indian government to promote solar energy.
 
• Besides Bhadla solar park, other significant solar projects in India include the **Pavagada Solar Park** in Karnataka and the **Rewa Solar Park** in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The development of solar parks and large-scale solar projects has attracted substantial investments and technological advancements in the renewable energy sector.
 
• India's solar energy sector has witnessed rapid growth, positioning the country as a global leader in solar power generation.
